## Cross-cutting invariants
Spine insert-only (no UPDATE/DELETE, and here no writes at all — every hosted statement ran in a
`READ ONLY` transaction as DB user `sig`); never a population total (named denominators); never a
fabricated count; secrets env-only (`PGPASSWORD` from Secret Manager, never on a command line or in a
file); no merge/tag/push-main; the Cloud SQL tier is not touched.

## Evidence report
**Summary.** The hosted OSM land is complete and verified: 1,214,682 `camreg_osm_surveillance` claims /
154,528 entities landed exactly once across the cancelled p964s (930,000) and the successful tjqdq
(+284,682) executions; the spine now holds **2,274,818 claims / 246,738 entities**. The earlier ≈2.43M
figure was a projection that counted the connector's 154,528 non-claim entity records. The settled
re-audit and the shaped intermediates are refreshed at as-of `2026-09-24T03:43:19Z` and frozen in
`LAUNCH_BASELINE_2026-09-24.md`.

**Gaps found after first implementation.** (1) The audit verb could not honestly produce a settled
report — its banner hard-coded "PROVISIONAL … may be in flight" → closed with the additive `--settled`
status (ADR-102). (2) The new ADR needed an Appendix F row + a BL mapping (`check_spec_src.py`,
`check_backlog.py` both failed until added) → closed. (3) A first BACKLOG.csv rewrite re-quoted two
unrelated rows → reverted to a single-row change.

**Deviations.** Idempotency is shown from the replay tjqdq already performed, not a new ingest (per the
orchestrator's instruction; evidence above). The Cloud SQL scale-up is an operator-approved deviation
recorded in ADR-102; the tier was not touched by this run.
